content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain what polymers and monomers are
Draw the structure of addition polymers from their monomers
Give examples of common addition polymers and their uses
are very large molecules made by joining together many small molecules called monomers. Addition polymers are formed when unsaturated monomers (containing C=C) join together in a chain reaction.
Small molecule that can join to form a polymer
Large molecule made from many monomers joined together
The process of joining monomers to make a polymer
Explore polymerisation — see how monomers join together to form addition and condensation polymers using the interactive visualisation below.
Monomers must contain a C=C double bond
No other product is formed (only polymer)

Explain what is meant by addition polymerisation.
Addition polymerisation is when many small unsaturated molecules (monomers) join together
The monomers contain C=C double bonds
The double bonds "open up" and monomers join end-to-end
A long chain polymer molecule is formed
No other product is formed (only the polymer)
This is different from condensation polymerisation, which produces a small molecule as well
State two uses of poly(ethene) and explain why it is suitable for these uses.
It is unreactive (doesn't react with contents)
It can be moulded into shape

The double bond opens up; polymer has only single bonds
